claim: A consumer app can import the built @byokit/pi entry and catch its typed PiError; the package is held back as private with Pi pinned to one exact version.

steps.start: a checkout with the package built, nothing else set up
steps: import the built @byokit/pi entry from a plain Node consumer
read the package's held-back flag and Pi pin
steps.result: the entry resolves to packages/pi/dist/index.js, exports PiError only, the package is private and pins Pi to 1.5.0

verdicts.seen: Read all five capture lines. They show package @byokit/pi 0.1.0 with private true and pi peer 1.5.0, resolves ./packages/pi/dist/index.js, exports PiError, and PiError true bad-id no such id. This supports the named outcome: the built entry exports a typed error, the package is private, and the Pi version is pinned.
